subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: What permanent public retry contract should OpenClaw expose for main LLM provider failures: provider-level retry config, agent/global retry config, both, or no new config surface?
rationale: The request adds a public config/API surface and changes provider fallback timing, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract or default retry semantics.

options.title: Approve one provider-level contract
options.body: Use a single provider-scoped retry block and require runtime wiring, idempotency limits, docs, schema updates, and upgrade proof before closing the issue.

options.title: Keep retries internal only
options.body: Handle only narrow transient overload cases in runtime policy and decline user-configurable retry knobs to keep config surface small.

options.title: Defer to broader routing work
options.body: Leave this issue open but make a broader provider routing/fallback item the canonical owner for retry, cooldown, and failure-class policy.

recommendation.title: Approve one provider-level contract
recommendation.body: Use a single provider-scoped retry block and require runtime wiring, idempotency limits, docs, schema updates, and upgrade proof before closing the issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across provider config and adjacent runtime/failover behavior.
